clue.text: Broach ideas involving rebuke

indicators.note: the phrase before it involves, or contains within its run of letters, the word wanted

blocks.note: found inside, spanning the join between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone raising ideas while scolding a colleague for them.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across broaCH IDEas.
explanation.definitionFit: To chide is to scold or tell off, a close synonym of the verb rebuke.

clue.text: Suspect piece of corn gathered in an ear

indicators.note: something taken in by an ear is heard rather than read, so go by sound

blocks.note: a kernel is one grain of corn, and the military rank is said the same way
troops mustered are gathered, and the condiment sounds much the same

explanation.surface: A dubious grain of corn found collected inside a cob.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Mustard is one of the suspects in the board game Clue (Cluedo in Britain). 'Ear' looks like an ear of corn but is the hearing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Mustard is a murder suspect in the detective board game Clue, so he is an example of a suspect.

clue.text: Dilapidated hotels stocking peeled fruit

indicators.note: peeling removes the skin, so the outer letters go and the core stays
stocking means holding goods inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: inns are small hotels
fruit without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Run-down hotels serving skinned fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: IN(RUI)NS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in ruins is wrecked and falling apart, which matches dilapidated as an adjective phrase.

clue.text: Beast disrupted the panel

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An animal burst in and broke up a panel discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant is a huge animal, an example of a beast.

clue.text: Pointed comments about kerfuffle in The Nation

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: barbs are sharp, wounding remarks
ado is fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: Sharp remarks about some fuss printed in The Nation magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: BARB(ADO)S. 'The Nation' looks like the magazine's own name, but the definition is any nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is an independent Caribbean island country, so it is an example of a nation.

clue.text: Bishop converted before the whole of life on Earth

definitions.text: the whole of life on Earth

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the word bishop, rearranged
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A bishop who converted before taking in all of life on the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' suits a bishop's religious work, but here it means rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The biosphere is the part of the planet where living things exist, taken as a whole system.

clue.text: Oddly, rail's near part of a staircase

indicators.note: oddly means take the letters in odd-numbered positions only

blocks.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Strangely, the handrail sits close to part of the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical board between two treads of a stair.

clue.text: Back streets: everything there is? Unfortunately, yes

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so the word after it is jumbled

blocks.note: all means everything
the word yes, jumbled

explanation.surface: A gloomy question about whether back streets are all there is, and the sad answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleys are narrow lanes behind buildings, the back streets of a town.

clue.text: Go in (taking the opposite in reverse order) to obtain result

indicators.text: taking the opposite in reverse order
indicators.note: each word is swapped for its opposite and the pair is then put in the other order

blocks.note: the opposite of in
the opposite of go

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting a result by doing the reverse of going in.
explanation.walkthrough: Go in becomes come out, and swapping the two words gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the way something turns out, its end result.

clue.text: Burglar penning a literary sequel?

blocks.note: the plain sense: a thief who climbs to an upper floor to break in
the joke sense: a writer producing a follow-up tale

explanation.surface: A burglar who also writes a follow-up novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage the second story is the floor above the ground floor, where this thief climbs in; read as a writer's second story it becomes a sequel.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-story man is American slang for a cat burglar who enters through upper windows.

clue.text: Astonishingly clear: no American is likely to steal

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; 'is likely to steal' describes a thieving nature

indicators.note: something done astonishingly is done in a startling, unexpected way, so the letters land in a surprising order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A clear statement that no American tends to be a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so a larcenous person is thieving, inclined toward stealing.

clue.text: Most of the second hot drink

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter

blocks.note: of two things named, the second is the latter

explanation.surface: Someone ordering a hot drink in the second round.
explanation.walkthrough: LATTER loses its last letter to leave LATTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso with steamed milk, a coffee served hot.

clue.text: In 7/8, music to a jockey's ears?

definitions.note: playful: the sound a horse makes

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle of the spoken form of the fraction, its ends cut away

blocks.note: the fraction written out in words

explanation.surface: A horse seven-eighths of the way round, its rider hearing sweet music.
explanation.walkthrough: The fraction 7/8 must be written out as words, sevEN EIGHths, before the answer appears; 7 and 8 look like references to other clues but are not.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the cry of a horse, the sound a jockey would cheerfully hear from a mount.

clue.text: Singer with a pop record initially in Mexico — and how!

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
in Mexico tells us to use Spanish words for the English ones that follow

blocks.note: 'a pop' means each, as in five dollars a pop, which is per
first letter of record
y is Spanish for and
como is Spanish for how

explanation.surface: A singer with a hit record, starting out in Mexico, and what a success!
explanation.walkthrough: PER + R + Y + COMO. 'And how!' reads as an exclamation but is two Spanish words, and 'a pop' is the American phrase for each.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry Como was an American crooner, famous for his relaxed baritone, so he is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Glee salons rocking Western city

indicators.note: rocking means shaking about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Cheerful bars swinging in a city out west.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles is the largest city in California, on the US west coast.

clue.text: Artificial language repeats "no" in a different way

indicators.note: a different way of arranging means the letters are reordered

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A constructed language that keeps saying no, but phrased differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto was invented by Zamenhof in 1887 as an international auxiliary tongue, the best-known constructed language.

clue.text: Dispatch Senate Democrat…

blocks.note: Sen. is the standard abbreviation
D labels a Democrat, as in D-NY

explanation.surface: An order to send off a Democratic senator, running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch something is to send it off to a destination.

clue.text: Casino employee with a more persistent cough

blocks.note: first meaning: the person running a gaming table
second meaning: the comparative of croupy, suffering from croup

explanation.walkthrough: Croup is a children's illness with a barking cough; croupy, croupier is a jokey comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier deals and collects stakes at a roulette or card table in a gambling house.

clue.text: …in the direction of university, not surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: U is the usual abbreviation for university
the word not, rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing from 15: send a senator off toward a university, which is no surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not surprisingly' reads as a stock phrase, but the not is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Unto is an old preposition meaning toward or to, showing direction of movement.

clue.text: Warm drops, red and meant for use on the skin

definitions.text: meant for use on the skin

indicators.note: drops means lets go of, so the following letter is removed

blocks.note: tropical describes hot, warm climates
R is short for red

explanation.surface: Warm red drops that are to be applied to the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: TROPICAL loses R. 'Drops' looks like liquid drops, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A topical medicine is applied to the body surface, such as a cream, rather than swallowed.

clue.text: Energize hairdo in time for tea

blocks.note: to pep up is to energize
a perm is a permanent-wave hairstyle
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Perk up a hairstyle in time for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time for tea' reads as one phrase; tea alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppermint is a popular herbal infusion, so it is a kind of tea.

clue.text: Opium is treacherous and unholy

indicators.note: treacherous suggests betrayal and disorder, so the letters are turned around

blocks.note: seven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A moral warning that opium is dangerous and sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, irreligious and wicked.

clue.text: Senior under 100 is not so hot

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed below, so it comes after

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
senior means older

explanation.surface: A centenarian-adjacent senior who is feeling less than great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so hot' sounds like 'not very good', but it is literal: less warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Colder is the comparative of cold, meaning lower in temperature, less warm.

clue.text: Two traditional toys are nearly maximum price

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word before it loses its end

blocks.note: a spinning top and a doll
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned toys now selling for almost the highest possible price.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying top dollar is an idiom for paying the highest amount, the top price.

clue.text: Liberal-sounding misses

indicators.note: sounding means as heard spoken, so go by pronunciation

blocks.note: lax means permissive or loose

explanation.surface: Political misses that sound liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lack something is to be without it, so lacks matches misses as a verb.

clue.text: Start dinner late with stimulant

indicators.note: start ... late means begin one letter in, so the first letter goes
with Start, a word that starts late has its opening letter cut

blocks.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Starting a meal late, helped by a stimulant.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPER started late becomes UPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper is slang for a stimulant drug such as an amphetamine, the opposite of a downer.

clue.text: Went swiftly, setting wheels in reverse ahead of vanden Heuvel

indicators.note: setting a vehicle in gear here means putting it into backward motion, paired with the words after
setting something in reverse means running it backward, so the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: wheels is slang for a car
Katrina vanden Heuvel was The Nation's editor, so she is ED

explanation.surface: Someone sped off, reversing the car in front of the magazine's editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Katrina vanden Heuvel edited The Nation; ED is the usual short form of editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced means moved at high speed, the past tense matching went swiftly.

clue.text: Blend of numeric writing from the ancient world

indicators.note: a blend mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into new order

blocks.note: seven letters of the fodder
two letters of the fodder

explanation.surface: A mixture of number-writing systems from antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuneiform is the wedge-shaped script of ancient Mesopotamia, pressed into clay tablets.

clue.text: Hitchcock's company lost 500 outside

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so a piece is taken away

blocks.note: the director's first name is Alfred, here possessive
D is the Roman numeral for 500
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Hitchcock's film studio lost money while shooting on location.
explanation.walkthrough: ALFRED'S minus D, then CO. 'Company' comes first in the clue but goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco means in the open air, borrowed from Italian, so it fits outside as an adverb.

clue.text: Amber, e.g., to transgress again?

blocks.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to sin is to transgress a moral law

explanation.surface: Is amber a substance for offending twice?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags reading the answer as RE-SIN, to sin again.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is fossilised tree resin, so it is one example of the substance.
